entities.summary:
Coursera, founded in 2012 by Stanford professors Andrew Ng and Daphne Koller, is a pioneering online education platform headquartered in Mountain View, California. It emerged in the context of the growing demand for accessible, high-quality education in an increasingly digital world, addressing the educational gaps present in both developed and developing regions. By partnering with leading universities and organizations worldwide, Coursera has democratized access to knowledge, impacting millions of learners across diverse demographics and geographies.

The platform launched with a handful of courses, rapidly expanding to offer thousands of courses across various disciplines, including computer science, data science, and humanities. As of 2023, Coursera boasts over 100 million registered users and collaborates with over 200 universities and companies, making it a critical player in the edtech industry. This transformation in education delivery has allowed learners to gain skills and certifications that are increasingly relevant in the modern workforce, thereby reshaping traditional educational paradigms.

Coursera's influence extends beyond individual learning; it has prompted institutions to reconsider their educational models. The rise of online learning catalyzed a shift in how knowledge is structured and delivered, pushing traditional universities to adopt hybrid formats and invest in digital infrastructure. This evolution has led to a broader acceptance of online credentials, challenging the status quo of conventional degrees and altering perceptions of educational value.

The impact of Coursera is evident in the statistic that by 2022, the global online education market was valued at over $250 billion, a testament to the lasting change initiated by platforms like Coursera. As Andrew Ng expressed, 'Education is the great equalizer,' underscoring the platform's mission to make quality learning accessible to all.
